janet_customer: Hi team — hitting a weird failure on /v1/rerank. Customer sent a payload and we get a 200 but ALL scores are 0, and sometimes a 422 when we try to flatten. Repro attached.
maria_cs: @jun_engineer tagging you. Customer says they migrated from an earlier client and now they pack 'query' inside each doc and also include a top-level query. payload below.

janet_customer: ```json
{
  \"query\": \"who wrote the book about inference\",
  \"candidates\": [
    {\"id\": \"c1\", \"text\": \"Redwood Inference: an intro\", \"score\": null},
    {\"id\": \"c2\", \"text\": \"Serving LLMs at scale\", \"score\": null}
  ],
  \"documents\": [
    {\"id\": \"c1\", \"passages\": [{\"text\": \"Redwood Inference: an intro\", \"query\": \"who wrote the book about inference\"}]},
    {\"id\": \"doc-2\", \"passages\": [{\"text\": \"Serving LLMs at scale\"}]}
  ]
}
```

janet_customer: They say their app expects the server to prefer candidate-level text when ids overlap, but it's returning zeros instead. Customer tried swapping order of candidates/docs, same result.

jun_engineer: Quick notes: the endpoint accepts either a flat candidates array OR a documents array with nested passages; mixing both is allowed but we have precedence rules — if ids collide between candidates and documents we currently treat the candidate array as authoritative for scoring. However there are two gotchas: 1) If you include per-passage \"query\" keys we accidentally trigger a path-match that bypasses the usual scoring route (bug logged), and 2) when both candidates and documents contain the same id but the text differs, we do a de-dup normalization that can result in score=0 if normalization yields an empty similarity vector (edge case).

jun_engineer: Repro steps I recommend: (1) remove all nested \"query\" keys from passages, (2) ensure ids across candidates/docs are unique OR remove the duplicate set and rely on one collection, (3) try the small curl below to see canonical behavior.

jun_engineer: ```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d ' {\"query\":\"who wrote the book about inference\",\"candidates\":[{\"id\":\"c1\",\"text\":\"Redwood Inference: an intro\"},{\"id\":\"c2\",\"text\":\"Serving LLMs at scale\"}] } ' 
```

maria_cs: Customer tested removing duplicates (they kept only candidates) and got proper non-zero scores. They still want to support documents+passages because their ingestion pipeline writes the nested shape.

jun_engineer: Ok — immediate mitigation: tell them to move the user query only to the top-level \"query\" and avoid per-passage query fields. We're pushing a small server-side validation that will 422 on mixed \"query\" placements with a clear error message. Longer term fix: we'll remove the accidental bypass path that zeroes scores when per-passage query is present and make id-collision behavior explicit. I've opened GH issue #RED-8723 and will post the patch PR there.

maria_cs: Noted. I'll relay to the customer: (1) short-term fix = dedupe ids OR remove nested \"query\"; (2) we can run a one-off migration script to flatten their docs into candidates if they want help; (3) we'll notify when the server validation and patch land. :thumbsup:

qa_bot: NOTE: added test case 'rerank_mixed_candidates_docs_query_location' to the regression suite, failing now (expected).

janet_customer: Thanks — removing nested queries fixed it on their staging. We'll wait for the validation change so we can catch it earlier. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :heart:
